purpose: One final presentation-stable finite-atlas accessibility comparison, not rank inference or a new retrospective campaign.
supplied_subgroups: M17 and M17+<Ei> for each original exceptional direction Ei; only targets outside the supplied subgroup are measured.
anchor_definition: Every nonzero Q in the supplied subgroup with canonical height(Q)<=H; include both signs and nonprimitive multiples.
height_convention: lim 4^(-n) h_x(2^n Q), natural logarithms, the larger/BSD convention used by Sage/PARI; never silently mix the half-height convention.
chart_normalization: The original curve model and exact raw slope (yP+yQ)/(xP-xQ), with the same curve-and-anchor-only N/F normalization as the sealed atlas; subgroup-independent.
output: Absolute best log2 parameter height and exact integer H(n:d), winning rational anchor and full word, complete chart count at each H, and target-level comparisons. Baseline drops are secondary.
metric_transport: Freeze one metric with rigorously justified error enclosures per original subgroup. Transport by exact integer congruence under each unimodular rebase; do not recompute or round entries. Use exact rational bounds for enumeration pruning and resolve membership at the H boundary by certified height intervals.
coverage_gate: A numerical positive-definite Gram matrix or a complete rounded-metric enumeration is insufficient. Require a certified lower bounding form and membership enclosures; unresolved boundary points imply UNKNOWN coverage. Chart evaluation must wait until coverage passes.
work_comparison: Report all three complete H-shell endpoints against chart count. Do not interpret a larger baseline drop as a better endpoint or a runtime speedup. If comparing equal-work prefixes, order anchors target-independently, with ties resolved by exact rational coordinates, never by basis words.
preflight_finding: The canonical atlas exposes numerical height entries but no certified uniform or entrywise canonical-height error enclosure. Decimal formatting and a symmetry check are not interval certificates. No canonical-height coverage claim is presently justified.
next_required_input: A rigorously bounded height metric and a replayable error-control argument. Do not substitute the rounded-metric short-vector certificate.
mathematical_claim: UNKNOWN canonical-height-ball comparison; no new chart arithmetic launched. This pending optional benchmark does not block equation-derived rank work.
